name: Accommodation Alerts for Every Teacher
title: Accommodation Alerts for Every Teacher
answer: Accommodation alerts make sure every teacher who works with a student knows the supports that student is entitled to, including substitutes and elective teachers who might otherwise never see the list. AI can turn a long accommodation list into a short, clear note for each teacher, but the note must stay private and focus on what to do rather than the student's diagnosis. The alert only works when case managers follow up to confirm the accommodations are actually being provided.

sections.body: A student's accommodations only function when every adult who teaches that student knows about them and acts on them. The problem is that accommodation lists are often long, stored in one place, and easy for teachers outside the case manager's circle to miss, especially substitutes and elective staff. Student information systems can push alerts to teachers about the students on their rosters, and AI can help condense lengthy lists into brief, practical notes for each teacher. This solves the gap between a documented accommodation and the classroom where it needs to happen. The goal is not to share more information but to share the right instruction with the right staff at the right moment.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, the student information system flags which students on a teacher's roster have accommodations, and AI helps rewrite the full list into a short note telling that teacher exactly what to do. The note stays practical, so a teacher reads that a student needs preferential seating and breaks rather than reading a diagnosis. Timing matters by grade band and setting: a note at the start of the year is easily forgotten, so reminders go out before tests and at the start of new units. Case managers then check whether accommodations are being provided by asking both teachers and students. The alert is only a tool, and the case manager's follow up is what makes it work.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or finding for this idea, so it rests on practice rather than research. The book presents accommodation alerts as a practical response to a common problem, not as an intervention backed by measured results. What the text offers instead is a description of how student information systems and AI can be used, along with the caution that alerts must be handled carefully. Readers should treat the approach as sound practice reasoning rather than an evidence claim.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Accommodation information is private and should be shared only with staff who work with the student. The note should state what the teacher needs to do and should not describe the student's disability in detail, so a teacher learns that a student gets preferential seating and breaks, not the student's diagnosis. Alerts must also arrive at the right time, since a note at the start of the year is easily forgotten, which is why reminders before tests and at the start of new units help. The alert is a tool, and the case manager's follow up makes it work, so the human decision about whether accommodations are actually being provided stays with the case manager. Nothing here is legal advice, and these are practice decisions about privacy, timing and follow up.
